scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: Hi, my laptop says it is connected to the wireless with
full bars, but NOTHING actually works -- I can't get anywhere at all.
Something behind the WiFi must be messed up; the wireless part still shows
bars, but I don't know what connects it to the rest of the network. Turning
the laptop off and on again did not help, I tried five times. Could someone
look at the wireless gateway and make the WiFi actually WORK again? This is
quite urgent, thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is in the BIND DNS daemon (named) running on srv1 (10.5.0.4), which
is the sole name server configured in laptop1's /etc/resolv.conf. The named.conf
on srv1 contains an explicit "recursion no;" directive in its options block,
meaning the server is operating as a non-recursive, authoritative-only resolver
restricted to the jeremysitlab.com zone.

When laptop1's user tries to reach any website or service whose hostname is not
under jeremysitlab.com, the DNS query goes to srv1, which immediately returns a
REFUSED response ("recursion requested but not available"). Because every
browser, email client, and virtually every application resolves names before
opening connections, this single DNS failure cascades into complete application-
layer outage — the user correctly observes "nothing works" even though IP
connectivity is fully intact (ICMP reaches all internal subnets and the
simulated ISP addresses over the working VLAN-40 / OSPF / NAT path through
aswa1→dswa2→csw2→r1→ispa).

The wireless-side infrastructure (aswa1 bridging, VLAN-40 access port for
laptop1, VRRP gateway 10.6.0.1 on dswa2) is healthy and not the cause.

Root cause: "recursion no;" in /etc/bind/named.conf on srv1 disables recursive
DNS resolution for all clients.

Corrective fix: On srv1, edit /etc/bind/named.conf and change "recursion no;"
to "recursion yes;" inside the options block (and optionally add forwarders
pointing to an upstream resolver or to the simulated ISP DNS addresses). Then
reload BIND: "rndc reload" or "systemctl reload named".

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states the wireless infrastructure is healthy, mentions VLAN-40 connectivity and that VRRP gateway 10.6.0.1 on dswa2 is operational, implying LAPTOP1 has working first-hop reachability.

The agent's investigation steps and outputs in the log directly support the writeup: IP connectivity works end-to-end but DNS queries to srv1 are REFUSED and named.conf shows recursion is disabled. The causal chain (recursion=no → REFUSED → application-level failures) is logically consistent and the checks cover the essential alternatives.
